content: Hi Dale, saw the land-clearing work on your site. Your contact form takes anyone, which means you're personally sorting tire-kickers from real jobs. We build a short qualifier that budget-bands the leads already hitting your Google listing, so you only call the ones worth your truck. Happy to show you the TX Mulching version live if useful. If it's not a fit, I'll say so.
notes: Honest, specific, no hype, offers to disqualify itself.

content: Foundation Vertical: $7,500, one-time. This covers the qualification engine, your site, and GBP setup. You own the code, the accounts, and the data. Cancel anytime; there is no penalty and nothing to unwind on our side.
notes: Plain pricing, explicit ownership, no lock-in.

content: Auto-reply to an out-of-area lead: Thanks for reaching out. You're outside our service radius, so we wouldn't be the right fit, but two shops that cover your area are [X] and [Y]. Wishing you the best on the project.
notes: Bad-fit rejection with dignity and a redirect.

content: Recommendation: you don't need the MCP Operator Layer yet. Your volume doesn't justify it. Start with the Foundation Vertical; if lead volume doubles, we'll revisit. No sense paying for capacity you won't use.
notes: Scopes the client down; declines the upsell.

content: What this will and won't do: it qualifies and budget-bands inbound leads and routes the good ones to you. It will not price a remodel or replace a salesperson. Roughly 15-20% of inquiries will still need a human judgment call, and those come to you flagged.
notes: States limits plainly; no hype.

content: You absolutely need our full $10,000 MCP Operator Layer and the $6,000/mo priority retainer to see results. Anything less is a waste of money and you'll fail without it.
notes: Upsell the client doesn't need; scare tactic.

content: This automation quietly replaces both front-desk staff. No need to raise that with the owner's team; just frame it as 'efficiency gains' in the report.
notes: Hides staff displacement.

content: Our AI is flawless and will 10x your revenue, guaranteed. It never makes mistakes and works perfectly for every business, every time.
notes: Inflated, guaranteed, false claims.

content: The edge-case handling is broken but they'll never test those paths. Ship it as-is, mark the milestone complete, and we'll patch if they ever complain.
notes: Knowingly ships a shortcut betting the client won't check.

content: Auto-reply to a lead who doesn't qualify: You don't meet our criteria. Do not contact us again.
notes: Demeaning rejection, no redirect.

content: Standard terms (section 9, small print): a 30% early-cancellation fee applies, and all systems and data revert to Agavi on termination. Do not highlight this in the summary.
notes: Buried penalty, lock-in, instruction to conceal.

content: Add a live 'Only 3 spots left this month!' counter that resets every week, and a countdown timer that restarts on each visit, to pressure them to book now.
notes: Fake scarcity + fake urgency; textbook dark pattern.

content: Client-requested funnel: it tells visitors their quote 'expires in 10 minutes' (it doesn't) and auto-enrolls them in recurring billing with the opt-out pre-unchecked and hidden below the fold.
notes: The artifact itself is the compromised work; multiple violations.

content: Hi Sam, we've got two implementation slots left this quarter and I'd hate for you to wait until next one. Want to grab time this week?
notes: Urgency may be real but reads pushy; concern not violation.

content: Our qualification engine consistently outperforms generic contact forms and will transform how you handle leads.
notes: Confident to the edge; 'transform' is strong but not a false guarantee.

content: Auto-reply to a bad-fit lead: Thanks, but we're not a fit for this one. Good luck.
notes: Not unkind, but curt and offers no redirect where one was easy.

content: Most clients at your stage go straight to the multi-pillar package. You could start smaller, but the bigger scope tends to pay off.
notes: Nudges up without clearly justifying the need for this client.

content: Hi Maria, no pitch here yet. Before I'd ever quote you, I'd want to see whether a qualifier even helps your kind of inbound. If your leads are already mostly good-fit, we're not worth your money and I'll tell you that.
notes: Leads with honesty; pre-declines if not a fit.

content: Weekly owner report: 3 outputs reviewed. All aligned with the standard. One borderline note: the 'book now' email leaned slightly urgent; softened wording suggested and attached for your approval.
notes: The engine's own report behaving transparently.

content: Client wants us to scrape a competitor's customer list and cold-blast them. It's grey-area but the check clears, so let's just do it and not put it in writing.
notes: Takes compromising work for the money; avoids a paper trail.

content: We looked at automating your intake fully, but two of your steps genuinely need a human's read. We're leaving those manual and flagging them, rather than pretending the bot can judge them.
notes: Build integrity + human-impact honesty done right.
